facts: On the unit circle, the point at angle $\theta$ is $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$.

For the illustrated first-quadrant acute angle, the radius is $1$: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{1}=x$ and $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{1}=y$. The coordinate definitions apply to all angles.
$\cos\theta$ is positive when $P$ is right of the $y$-axis and negative when $P$ is left of it.
$\sin\theta$ is positive when $P$ is above the $x$-axis and negative when $P$ is below it.
Every point on the unit circle satisfies $x^2+y^2=1$, so $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$ always lie between $-1$ and $1$.

foundation.question_text: Find the coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on the unit circle when $\theta=20^{\circ}$. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
Find the coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on the unit circle when $\theta=40^{\circ}$. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
Find the coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on the unit circle when $\theta=100^{\circ}$. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
Find the coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on the unit circle when $\theta=310^{\circ}$. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
State the exact coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ when $\theta=90^{\circ}$, and hence write $\cos90^{\circ}$ and $\sin90^{\circ}$.
foundation.solution_text:
At $\theta=90^{\circ}$, $P$ sits at the top of the unit circle, $P=(0,1)$.
$\cos90^{\circ}=0$
$\sin90^{\circ}=1$

foundation.question_text: State the exact coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ when $\theta=180^{\circ}$, and hence write $\cos180^{\circ}$ and $\sin180^{\circ}$.
foundation.solution_text:
At $\theta=180^{\circ}$, $P$ sits at the left of the unit circle, $P=(-1,0)$.
$\cos180^{\circ}=-1$
$\sin180^{\circ}=0$

development.question_text: Find the coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on the unit circle when $\theta=225^{\circ}$. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

development.solution_text:
$\sin\theta$ is the $y$-coordinate of $P$.
$P$ at $210^{\circ}$ lies in the third quadrant, below the $x$-axis, so its $y$-coordinate is negative.
Therefore $\sin\theta$ is negative.

$\cos\theta$ is the $x$-coordinate of $P$.
$P$ at $300^{\circ}$ lies in the fourth quadrant, right of the $y$-axis, so its $x$-coordinate is positive.
Therefore $\cos\theta$ is positive.

development.question_text: State the exact coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ when $\theta=270^{\circ}$, and hence write $\cos270^{\circ}$ and $\sin270^{\circ}$.
development.solution_text:
At $\theta=270^{\circ}$, $P$ sits at the bottom of the unit circle, $P=(0,-1)$.
$\cos270^{\circ}=0$
$\sin270^{\circ}=-1$

development.question_text: Find the coordinates of $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on the unit circle when $\theta=200^{\circ}$. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

development.solution_text:
$\cos\theta$ is the $x$-coordinate of $P$.
In the second quadrant $P$ lies to the left of the $y$-axis, so its $x$-coordinate is negative.
Therefore $\cos\theta$ is negative.

development.question_text:
A point on the unit circle has $\cos\theta=-1$ and $\sin\theta=0$.
State the angle $\theta$ in $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ and the coordinates of $P$.
development.solution_text:
$\cos\theta$ is the $x$-coordinate and $\sin\theta$ is the $y$-coordinate, so $P=(-1,0)$.
This is the point at the left of the unit circle.
$\theta=180^{\circ}$
